title: Shipment Timing Limits Across the PAP Supply Replenishment Program Schedules
content:
Each resupply schedule of the PAP Supply Replenishment Program sets how early a new shipment of an item may go out, how many months of supply one shipment of an item may cover, whether quantities not shipped in an earlier period may be added to a later shipment, and how many extra days early a shipment may go out when the patient will be traveling.

| Schedule | Ship-window days (most calendar days before the covered-through date of the item's last shipped line that a new shipment of that item may go out) | Most months of supply per shipment of an item | Missed-cycle quantities may be added to a later shipment | Extra early days for travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicare Part B Resupply Schedule | 10 | 3 | no | 0 (not allowed) |
| Medicare Advantage Resupply Schedule | 10 | 3 | no | 0 (not allowed) |
| Medicaid Resupply Schedule | 10 | 1 | no | 0 (not allowed) |
| Commercial HMO Resupply Schedule | 10 | 3 | no | 14 |
| Commercial PPO Resupply Schedule | 10 | 3 | no | 14 |
| Self-Pay Supply Subscription | 30 | 3 | yes | 30 |

A travel allowance of 0 means that going out early for travel is not allowed on that schedule.

## Distinguishing the schedules

- The Medicaid Resupply Schedule allows at most 1 month of supply per shipment of an item; every other schedule allows 3.
- The Self-Pay Supply Subscription is the only schedule with a 30-day ship window and the only one on which missed-cycle quantities may be added to a later shipment.
- Travel adds 14 days on the two commercial schedules and 30 days on the Self-Pay Supply Subscription; the Medicare Part B, Medicare Advantage and Medicaid schedules allow none.
